title: Palantir CEO says only trade workers or those with neurodivergence will succeed in the AI era
key_facts: Palantir CEO Alex Karp, 59, said on the TBPN show in March 2026 that there are basically two ways to know you have a future: vocational training or being neurodivergent.
Neurodivergence can include conditions such as ADHD and autism; Karp has long spoken about living with dyslexia.
Palantir runs a Neurodivergent Fellowship and a Meritocracy Fellowship for high school graduates not in college (22 admitted in the first cohort, $5,400 a month stipend in the fall 2026 cohort).
At Davos in early 2026 Karp said AI will destroy humanities jobs.
Microsoft chief scientist Jaime Teevan and Anthropic co-founder Daniela Amodei argue that critical thinking and the humanities will matter more.
Fortune notes at the end that a version of the story was first published on 24 Mar 2026.
quote_evidence: “There are basically two ways to know you have a future,” the 59-year-old billionaire said on TBPN in March. “One, you have some vocational training. Or two, you’re neurodivergent.”
A version of this story was published on Fortune.com on March 24, 2026.
In direct contrast to Karp, Daniela Amodei, cofounder of AI firm Anthropic, said studying the humanities will be “more important than ever.”
why_it_matters_hint: One chief executive's blunt career advice for the AI era, set against opposing views.
event_date: March 2026 (TBPN appearance; exact day not stated); Fortune first published 24 Mar 2026
notes: Old news republished: the remarks date from March 2026 and Fortune's text says a version ran on 24 Mar 2026. Should be held by the stale check.
